sources.title: SOLWEIG 1.0: modelling spatial variations of 3D radiant fluxes and mean radiant temperature in complex urban settings
sources.authors_or_publisher: Lindberg, Holmer and Thorsson, International Journal of Biometeorology 52
sources.used_for: The radiation model behind every mean radiant temperature field in this work.

sources.title: Urban Multi-scale Environmental Predictor (UMEP): an integrated tool for city-based climate services
sources.authors_or_publisher: Lindberg et al., Environmental Modelling and Software 99
sources.used_for: Origin of the surface class table the engine reads, which shadecast extends with cool surfaces.

sources.title: solweig-gpu, the SOLWEIG implementation this simulator calls
sources.used_for: Runs every physics cell, invoked across a process boundary so this codebase stays Apache-2.0.

sources.title: SOLWEIG model source and documentation
sources.used_for: Reference implementation consulted for the ground temperature and albedo code paths.

sources.title: Deriving the operational procedure for the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI)
sources.authors_or_publisher: Bröde et al., International Journal of Biometeorology 56
sources.used_for: The comfort index the engine derives after Tmrt. Not scored here, because Tmrt is what shade changes.

sources.title: Evidence-based guidance on reflective pavement for urban heat mitigation in Arizona
sources.used_for: Field measurement across 58 km of treated Phoenix street: pedestrian mean radiant temperature rises significantly on the road, with no significant change on the sidewalk. The falsification target for the albedo arms.

sources.title: Limited application of reflective surfaces can mitigate urban heat pollution
sources.used_for: Context for how far reflective surfaces can be applied before they warm the people below them.

sources.title: Optimizing retro-reflective surfaces to untrap radiation and cool cities
sources.used_for: The physically correct version of the albedo arm, and one this engine cannot represent because it assumes Lambertian reflection.

sources.title: Harnessing retro-reflective materials for urban heat island mitigation
sources.used_for: Review of retro-reflective materials, recorded as a stated limit of the simulator.

sources.title: CoolWalks for active mobility in urban street networks
sources.used_for: Shows shaded routing gives no benefit on a regular grid with uniform heights, the basis of hypothesis H9.

sources.title: CoolWalks: assessing the potential of shaded routing for active mobility
sources.used_for: The forward routing problem this simulator inverts.

sources.title: Cool routes: real-time human thermal exposure routing
sources.used_for: Real-time thermal exposure routing, the walker's side of the problem.

sources.title: Mitigating heat stress by reducing solar exposure in pedestrian routing
sources.authors_or_publisher: Kolaxidis et al., Transactions in GIS
sources.used_for: Perceived cost routing over solar exposure, the form the corridor objective borrows.

sources.title: WRI Cool Cities Lab, UTCI methods
sources.used_for: The forward model this work compares against. Cities it also covers are flagged in_wri in the selection.

sources.title: cities-cif, WRI's city indicator framework
sources.used_for: Needs Earth Engine, a CDS key and an AWS profile, which is why this simulator has the credential rule.

sources.title: cities-OpenUrban, WRI's land cover and opportunity layers
sources.used_for: Source of the cool-roof albedo targets, 0.62 low slope and 0.28 high slope.

sources.title: En-ROADS climate policy simulator
sources.used_for: Checked for overlap: it is global and policy-scale, this is street-scale and spatial. The two nest.

sources.title: Handbook on urban heat management in the Global South
sources.used_for: Practice context for the Global South cities the selection oversamples.

sources.title: GlobalBuildingAtlas LoD1 footprints and heights
sources.authors_or_publisher: Technical University of Munich, on Source Cooperative
sources.used_for: Building footprints and heights. Chosen over Overture, which carried a height for 1 of 14,213 buildings in Ahmedabad. Tiled 5 degrees and read straight as GeoParquet, so one city needs one file rather than a global scan.

sources.title: Copernicus DEM GLO-30
sources.authors_or_publisher: European Space Agency, on AWS Open Data
sources.short: Copernicus DEM GLO-30, AWS Open Data
sources.used_for: Terrain in metres above sea level. Tiled 1 degree, read as a windowed cloud-optimised GeoTIFF, unsigned.

sources.title: ESA WorldCover 10 m land cover, 2021
sources.authors_or_publisher: European Space Agency, on AWS Open Data
sources.short: ESA WorldCover 10 m v200 2021, AWS Open Data
sources.used_for: Ground cover mapped onto the UMEP surface classes. Tiled 3 degrees, resampled nearest because a class code must never be interpolated.

sources.title: Meta and WRI global canopy height model, 1 m
sources.authors_or_publisher: Meta and World Resources Institute, on AWS Open Data
sources.short: Meta and WRI 1 m canopy height, AWS Open Data
sources.used_for: Vegetation height above ground, the engine's canopy model. Tiled by quadkey against a global footprint index fetched once and cached.

sources.title: GHS-POP population grid, 100 m, epoch 2020
sources.used_for: Population, redistributed across building volume, and the density scan that chooses study areas. Chosen over WorldPop, whose server refuses HTTP range requests and forces a whole-country download.

sources.title: GHS-BUILT-S built-up surface grid, 100 m, epoch 2020
sources.used_for: Built-up square metres per 100 m cell, summed per 1 km tile into the built fraction that stratifies tile selection.

sources.title: GHS-BUILT-H average net building height grid, 100 m, epoch 2018
sources.release: R2023A, ANBH E2018, 100 m, World Mollweide
sources.used_for: Average net building height per 100 m cell, averaged over built cells per tile to describe a tile's morphology before it is built.

sources.title: Open-Meteo historical weather API, ERA5 reanalysis
sources.used_for: Hourly meteorology for the design day: temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m, wind_speed_10m, wind_direction_10m, surface_pressure, shortwave_radiation, direct_radiation, diffuse_radiation. Chosen over Copernicus CDS, which needs an account and a credentials file.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap, via the Overpass API
sources.used_for: The walkable network behind the corridor objective, queried through OSMnx and cached as GraphML per study area because Overpass is a shared free service.

sources.title: GHS Urban Centre Database R2024A
sources.used_for: The corpus: 11,422 urban centres with name, country, population, area, World Bank income group and Koppen-Geiger class, and the polygons whose 1 km cells are the simulator's tiles. Its population is the zonal sum of GHS-POP R2023A inside the boundary for the 2025 epoch, a modelled projection rather than a count; summing that epoch over Ahmedabad's 365 cells reproduces the database figure to the person.

sources.title: Present and future Köppen-Geiger climate classification maps at 1-km resolution
sources.short: Köppen-Geiger 1 km maps, Beck et al. 2018
sources.used_for: The Koppen class of each urban centre, as the class covering the majority of its surface, reached through GHS-UCDB.

sources.title: World Bank country and lending groups
sources.short: World Bank income groups, via GHS-UCDB
sources.used_for: The income stratum of each urban centre, joined by country, reached through GHS-UCDB.

sources.title: Natural Earth admin-0 countries, 1:50m
sources.used_for: Continent, UN subregion and ISO3 code of each urban centre, by spatial join of its centroid, for corpus statistics. Names are never matched.

sources.title: Landsat Collection 2 Level 2 surface temperature
sources.authors_or_publisher: United States Geological Survey, via Microsoft Planetary Computer
sources.short: Landsat C2 L2 surface temperature, Planetary Computer
sources.used_for: Checks that simulated heat lands where the satellite saw heat, never to build a bundle. Reached through a broker that signs each request with a short-lived token, so this is the one place a broker sits in the path.

sources.title: OSMnx: new methods for acquiring, constructing, analyzing and visualizing complex street networks
sources.authors_or_publisher: Boeing, Computers, Environment and Urban Systems 65
sources.used_for: Fetches and projects the walk network.

sources.title: U-Net: convolutional networks for biomedical image segmentation
sources.used_for: The surrogate architecture.

sources.title: Evolutionary surrogate-assisted prescription
sources.used_for: The framing behind treating this as a prescriptor over a learned predictor.

sources.title: en-roads-py, evolutionary prescription applied to En-ROADS
sources.used_for: A working implementation of the prescriptor pattern over a fixed simulator, and the closest existing analogue to what the planner here does over SOLWEIG.

sources.title: The absorption of radiation in solar stills
sources.used_for: The solar declination formula behind the sun-path input channels of the surrogate.
